$comment: COPY THIS, then delete every $comment. Files beginning with '_' are skipped
by `tcat-validate all`, which is why this template can carry comments and
REPLACE placeholders without failing CI. Your copy must not start with '_'.
THE ONE THING PEOPLE GET WRONG: use the time-indexed form below even when you
have exactly one entry. A fixed calibration is the degenerate case of a
drifting one. Written this way, the day you have a before/after bracket you
append a second entry and nothing downstream changes. Written as a flat set of
numbers, every consumer grows a special case -- and those special cases are
what break when the second entry arrives.
Generate calibration_id; do not name it:
A hand-written label like 'our-calibration-v2' could be edited in place, and
then nothing downstream could tell which fits went stale.
$comment_kind: ms_sensitivity | ir_reference | xas_reference | flow | temperature | other.
Note that ir_reference and xas_reference exist: background subtraction and
reference-spectrum selection are TRANSFORMATIONS with their own artifacts, not
silent preprocessing. If your instrument software already did one, it still
needs to be captured here or the provenance chain has a hole in it.
$comment_owner: Everything downstream depends on calibration code, so a change here is
reviewed by whoever owns the instrument -- not by whoever is available.

entries.notes: REPLACE -- how this was determined, and what its known limits are.

$comment_entries: valid_from must be UTC with an explicit offset. Entries ascend.
sensitivity_sigma is not optional in practice. Calibration uncertainty
propagates but belongs to neither data nor parameter uncertainty -- omit it and
every derived trace looks more certain than it is, invisibly.
units are written target-over-source so the conversion is checkable by
inspection rather than by reading code.
valid_range is the signal range this factor was measured over. Extrapolating
outside it is a judgement call that should be visible.
fragmentation_matrix_ref: for MS, 'art://frag-<id>'. A cited artifact, not an
inline table, because the cracking pattern is revised independently of the
sensitivities. For a real propane-ODH product slate you WILL need one --
propane, propene, CO, CO2, and O2 share m/z channels, and per-channel
sensitivities alone give systematically wrong concentrations.
determined_from: the calibration-gas or standard dataset ids this was fit
from. Makes the calibration itself auditable.
$comment_supersedes: art://<previous-calibration-id>, if any. An explicit chain, rather than
leaving a reader to sort by date and guess.
$comment_immutability: A calibration change produces a NEW artifact with a NEW id. It never mutates
an existing one. That is what makes it possible to swap one id and re-derive
every affected trace -- and what lets `tcat-provenance --reverse` name exactly
